introduction.definition: A waste heat recovery boiler (HRSG) makes steam from hot exhaust gas — for example from a gas turbine, engine, kiln or furnace. The gas passes the superheater, evaporator and economizer in turn; water circulates naturally between the steam drum and the evaporator tubes.
applications: Combined-cycle power plants (gas turbine + steam turbine)
Cement kilns, glass furnaces, sulphuric acid plants
key_points: Pinch and approach temperatures set recovery
Low-temperature end limited by dew point
introduction.summary: A waste heat recovery boiler (heat recovery steam generator, HRSG) makes steam from the hot exhaust of a gas turbine, engine, furnace or kiln. The gas passes superheater, evaporator and economizer banks in turn; water/steam circulates naturally between the drum and evaporator.

temperature.title: Gas temperature profile through the HRSG
temperature.description: Exhaust gas gives up heat to the superheater, then the evaporator, then the economizer. The smallest gas-to-water temperature difference — the pinch point at the evaporator outlet — and the approach temperature at the economizer outlet set how much heat can be recovered (typical design pinch ~ 8–15 °C).

foundation: Level concrete plinth/foundation designed for operating weight full of water; allow access for tube cleaning and burner maintenance.
alignment: Level the boiler; align burner and fan; check expansion allowances on headers and casings.
piping: Fit safety valves with unobstructed discharge piped to a safe place; feedwater with check and isolation valves; blowdown to a blowdown vessel.
Flue/stack sized for the draught required; explosion relief where specified.
commissioning: Boil-out/chemical clean; hydro-test; set and test safety valves; test low-water cut-outs and flame safeguard (purge, ignition, flame failure); tune combustion (O₂, CO).

routine.task: Monitor drum level, pinch and stack temperature.

overhaul.task: Inspect tubes and headers; casing liners.

lubrication: No lubrication for the static parts — lubricate valve stems, rotating parts and drives per maker.

causes: Low pH, low oxygen, high velocity

remedies: Controlled ramp rates; design for cycling

safety: Gas bypass/diverter interlocks; drum safety valves; purge before GT start.

video_tutorials.title: Waste Heat Recovery Boiler — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Waste Heat Recovery Boiler.
A waste heat recovery boiler (HRSG) makes steam from hot exhaust gas — for example from a gas turbine, engine, kiln or furnace.
The gas passes the superheater, evaporator and economizer in turn; water circulates naturally between the steam drum and the evaporator tubes.
Typical applications include combined-cycle power plants (gas turbine + steam turbine); cogeneration (CHP); cement kilns, glass furnaces, sulphuric acid plants.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Insulated Gas Casing & Inlet Transition (from turbine/kiln exhaust), Outlet Transition & Stack.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Waste Heat Recovery Boiler — Operation

script.narration: How the Waste Heat Recovery Boiler works.
Hot exhaust gas enters through the inlet transition.
The superheater meets the hottest gas.
The evaporator boils water; steam–water mixture rises to the drum.
The drum separates steam; downcomers feed water back.
The economizer heats feedwater in the coolest gas before the stack.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Exhaust gas gives up heat to the superheater, then the evaporator, then the economizer.

video_tutorials.title: Waste Heat Recovery Boiler — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Waste Heat Recovery Boiler.
Monitor drum level, pinch and stack temperature.
Water chemistry; FAC inspections.
Inspect tubes and headers; casing liners.
Watch for flow-accelerated corrosion: thinning in economizer/evaporator. Common cause: low ph, low oxygen, high velocity.
Watch for thermal fatigue: header cracks. Common cause: frequent starts (cycling).
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
